webster.text: Natural aversion; instinctive contrariety or opposition in feeling; an aversion felt at the presence, real or ideal, of a particular object.

example.quote: RANDOLPH, notwithstanding his antipathy to paper money, could not agree to strike out the words, as he could not foresee all the occasions which might arise.
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, August 16, 1787
